planting.note: Set out rooted cuttings or nursery starts after frost danger passes in well-drained, moderately fertile soil in full sun; this vigorous selection from the UC Botanical Garden at Berkeley shrugs off Gulf South heat and humidity better than many baby sage forms.

directions: This exceptionally floriferous baby sage selection carries rich magenta-purple flowers noticeably larger than the species type, packed densely along the stems from spring through hard frost with only brief pauses in peak summer heat. Give it full sun and well-drained soil; it forms a rounded, well-branched mound and is a superb hummingbird and bee plant for a mixed border or pollinator bed. Shear lightly after each flush to keep growth dense and encourage rebloom, and take cuttings in fall as insurance since plants can decline in cold, wet winter soil.

common_name: Pozo Blue Sage (Pozo Blue Hybrid Cleveland Sage)

planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in spring into lean, sharply drained soil in full sun; this natural hybrid between Salvia clevelandii and S. leucophylla is more vigorous and larger-growing than either parent, so give it plenty of room and avoid heavy clay or summer irrigation.

directions: A vigorous, large-growing hybrid Cleveland sage discovered along Pozo Road in San Luis Obispo County, prized for its intensely fragrant gray-green foliage and dense whorls of soft lavender-blue flowers held well above the foliage in late spring and early summer. It draws bees, butterflies, and hummingbirds in numbers and is deer- and rabbit-resistant once established. In Gulf South gardens it demands raised beds or gritty, mounded soil for sharp drainage since prolonged humidity and wet feet are its main limiting factors, not cold; skip supplemental irrigation once roots are established.

common_name: Allen Chickering Sage (Allen Chickering Hybrid Cleveland Sage)

planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in spring into lean, sharply drained soil in full sun; named for Allen Chickering, a founder of the former Rancho Santa Ana Botanic Garden, this is one of the oldest and most widely grown Cleveland sage hybrids.

directions: Introduced in the 1960s-70s, this classic hybrid between Salvia clevelandii and S. leucophylla forms a rounded, fast-growing shrub with intensely aromatic, wrinkled gray-green leaves and dense, whorled clusters of violet-blue flowers in late spring. It is one of the most reliable and commercially available Cleveland sage selections, valued for strong fragrance, vigor, and heavy bee, butterfly, and hummingbird traffic during bloom. As with other clevelandii hybrids, success in humid Gulf South gardens depends on sharp drainage and lean soil rather than winter cold, which it tolerates well down to the mid-teens Fahrenheit.

planting.note: Set out rooted cuttings or container plants after frost danger passes in well-drained, moderately fertile soil in full sun; this Huntington Botanical Garden hybrid of Salvia clevelandii and S. leucantha inherits far better heat and humidity tolerance from its Mexican bush sage parent than pure clevelandii types.

directions: This graceful hybrid between Cleveland sage and Mexican bush sage produces long, gently arching spikes of soft lavender-pink flowers cradled in purple-gray calyxes over aromatic, felted gray-green foliage, blooming heavily from summer into fall with only a brief pause at the height of peak heat. Unlike straight Cleveland sage, Waverly tolerates the humidity and clay-heavy soils common in Gulf South gardens reasonably well as long as drainage is adequate, making it a good bridge plant between the dry-climate clevelandii hybrids and the heat-loving leucantha types. It is an excellent hummingbird and bee plant; cut the woody stems back hard after winter dieback to renew growth each spring.

planting.note: Set out nursery starts after frost danger has passed in well-drained, amended beds or large containers; a sister selection to Wendy's Wish and Ember's Wish from the same Australian breeding program, it blooms continuously through hot, humid Gulf Coast summers.

directions: A compact, mounding hybrid sage bred as part of the same Australian 'Wishes' series as Wendy's Wish and Ember's Wish, carrying rich wine-purple flowers with near-black calyces held on well-branched stems from spring straight through to frost. Because it is a sterile hybrid that sets no seed, energy goes entirely into flower production rather than seed set, giving an unusually long and dense bloom display that draws hummingbirds, butterflies, and bees. It handles Gulf South heat and humidity well in full sun with consistent moisture and good drainage; cut back hard in late winter to renew growth, and take softwood cuttings in fall since plants can be short-lived in wet, cold winter soil.
